core.text: Keep eight initial notices fixed: six registrations and seven distinct recognitions remain. Registration enables requests but is independently measured. Later status-query demand is a hypothesis; no new demand occurs in this window.

Interrupt the hypothesized teaching signal by suppressing receipts for already recognized identities. Validate N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 0,1,2,3,4,5. Request individually N2,N3,N4,N5,N6 at ticks 0,1,2,3,4; bulk N7,N8 at tick 6. Predicted deliveries: N2 through N6 at ticks 1 through 5, N7 at 7, N8 at 8. This removes repeat exposure to N1 while retaining the required receipt link.

Closest rival/sham retains the same validation sequence and dashboard reconciliation but does not suppress recognized N1: bulk at 0; individual N3,N4,N5,N6 at 2,3,4,5; bulk N7,N8 at 6. Predicted deliveries are duplicate N1 at 1, N2 at 2, N3 through N6 at 3 through 6, N7 at 7, N8 at 8. Both traces predict eight registrations, eight recognitions and six actions; the sham preserves one repeated receipt and two bulk signals.

residue.text: Feasible separating probe for present exposure: independently replay the two finite schedules and compare ledger counts, duplicate IDs, successful delivery times and dashboard states. Any missing registration, recognition below eight, seventh action, or duplicate in the interruption defeats its operational claim. This probe verifies interruption versus sham; it cannot distinguish later-demand accounts because later demand is excluded.

Each schedule uses six registration-clerk ticks and six dispatcher actions; ledger reads add no clerk labor. Interruption consumes seven delivery slots, sham eight. No extra server, channel, repair or configuration is available. No successful execution is observed.

Delay origin, sender adaptation and a globally best schedule remain unknown. Retain both causal accounts through distillation. A hypothetical later comparison would need independently attributable new status-query notices and comparable sender conditions; neither observation nor intervention on later demand is available here. Equal later demand despite verified exposure reduction would oppose the induced-demand account; a difference would still require excluding exogenous differences.

tension.account_a: Exogenous later-demand account: later status queries arise independently of receipt frequency.
tension.account_b: Tool-induced later-demand account: repeated bulk receipt exposure teaches senders to submit additional status-query notices.
tension.prediction_a: If comparable later observations existed, interruption and sham would have similar added demand despite different repeated-receipt exposure. Both predict zero added demand in this stipulated window.
tension.prediction_b: If comparable later observations existed, interruption would reduce added demand among affected senders relative to sham. This is unobserved and does not predict present extra demand.
